name: thyroid function pathway
title: Thyroid function pathway: TSH case-finds and free T4 confirms; hypothyroidism splits into primary (Hashimoto's), subclinical and central by TSH and free T4; thyrotoxicosis splits on radioactive iodine uptake into Graves, toxic nodules and thyroiditis or exogenous hormone, plus subclinical hyperthyroidism; each column gives causes and clues, tests and treatment

nodes.title: Thyroid function: TSH case-finds, free T4 (± T3) confirms
lines: primary disease is commonest: TSH moves OPPOSITE the hormone
central disease is the trap: TSH moves WITH it, or not at all

nodes.title: HYPOTHYROID: too little thyroid hormone
lines: TSH ↑ (primary) · up to 2% · female 5–8 : 1

nodes.title: THYROTOXIC: too much thyroid hormone, from any cause
lines: TSH ↓ · up to 1.5% · female 5 : 1 · hyperthyroidism = from PRODUCTION

nodes.title: Presents as
lines: COLD intolerance · weight GAIN despite ↓ appetite
fatigue, slow mentation, apathy, depression · constipation · cool, pale skin
bradycardia · diastolic hypertension, NARROW pulse pressure · ↓ cardiac output
slow RELAXATION of the reflexes · short of breath, heart failure

nodes.title: Presents as
lines: HEAT intolerance, sweating · weight LOSS despite ↑ appetite
hyperactivity, insomnia, anxiety, emotional lability · hyperdefecation · soft, warm skin · TREMOR
tachycardia · WIDE pulse pressure · ↑ cardiac output · palpitations · heart failure
eyes in ANY thyrotoxicosis: stare, lid retraction, lid lag
urgent: storm / instability (Graves) · high-output failure · visual loss · mental health crisis

nodes.title: Confirm (repeat ↓TSH + ↑FT4 + ↑FT3), then: is the gland MAKING it or LEAKING it?
lines: RAI uptake + scan: the best single test for the cause · 2-day test · expensive · NOT in pregnancy
~TRAb blood test is sensitive and specific for Graves

nodes.title: Primary hypothyroidism
lines: TSH ↑ · FT4 ↓
commonest: HASHIMOTO's

nodes.title: Subclinical hypothyroidism
lines: TSH ↑ · FT4 + FT3 normal
up to 10% · TSH usually < 10–20

nodes.title: Central hypothyroidism
lines: TSH ↔ or ↓ · FT4 ↓
PITUITARY or hypothalamus

nodes.title: Graves disease
lines: the COMMONEST cause
TSH-receptor antibodies drive it

nodes.title: Toxic adenoma / multinodular goiter
lines: autonomous nodule(s)
TMNG = toxic multinodular goiter

nodes.title: Thyroiditis or exogenous
lines: LOW uptake: hormone LEAKING
out of a damaged gland, or from a bottle

nodes.title: Subclinical hyperthyroidism
lines: TSH ↓ · FT4 + FT3 normal
same causes as overt

nodes.title: Hashimoto's thyroiditis
lines: female · family history of autoimmune disease · iodine load
~symptoms variable, signs not sensitive

nodes.title: Other causes
lines: drugs: lithium, amiodarone · surgery or radioactive iodine

nodes.title: No treatment history, no pituitary risk
lines: → you may simply ASSUME Hashimoto's

nodes.title: Often resolves on its own
lines: especially TSH < 10 in the elderly

nodes.title: Suspect it with
lines: other pituitary deficiencies or a known pituitary mass

nodes.title: Causes
lines: ↓ stimulation: trauma, surgery, tumour, infiltrative disease

nodes.title: Risk factors
lines: female · age ~30–50 · family history of autoimmune (esp. thyroid) · iodine load

nodes.title: Acute or subacute
lines: new neck mass

nodes.title: Graves only: orbitopathy, dermopathy
lines: proptosis, periorbital edema, diplopia · VISUAL LOSS = ocular emergency · SMOKING the major risk

nodes.title: Risk factors
lines: iodine deficiency moving to sufficiency, or an iodine load

nodes.title: Gradually progressive
lines: MILDLY thyrotoxic · neck mass(es)

nodes.title: Subacute (post-viral)
lines: recent upper respiratory infection · tender, PAIN, odynophagia

nodes.title: Post-partum or autoimmune
lines: also radiation, trauma

nodes.title: Exogenous
lines: over-treatment, factitious

nodes.title: Goiter
lines: asymmetric, symmetric or NONE

nodes.title: Linked to
lines: bone loss · atrial fibrillation

nodes.title: Rarely assay interference
lines: look up interfering substances, repeat TSH + FT4/FT3

nodes.title: CONFIRM: repeat ↑TSH + ↓FT4
lines: free T3 not needed

nodes.title: Leave these alone
lines: anti-TPO, anti-thyroglobulin: rarely change decisions · ultrasound: only for a nodule felt on exam

nodes.title: Repeat TSH + FT4
lines: TSH ↑ with normal free hormone

nodes.title: Higher risk of progression
lines: TSH > 10 · anti-TPO positive

nodes.title: Order TSH + FT4 TOGETHER
lines: here TSH moves WITH the hormone, or not at all: a normal TSH does NOT reassure

nodes.title: TSH receptor antibody (TRAb)
lines: sensitive AND specific · a blood test · not covered by OHIP

nodes.title: RAI uptake + scan
lines: DIFFUSE high uptake

nodes.title: RAI uptake + scan
lines: ONE hot nodule (adenoma) · SEVERAL (TMNG)

nodes.title: RAI uptake LOW
lines: almost none on the scan

nodes.title: Levothyroxine once daily
lines: about 1.5 mcg/kg/day, titrated to a normal TSH
start LOW if elderly or heart disease

nodes.title: Half-life 1 WEEK
lines: TSH every 4–6 weeks until normal · don't follow FT4/FT3 on replacement

nodes.title: How to take it
lines: ≥ 1 h before, ≥ 2 h after food · 4 h from calcium, iron, magnesium, multivitamin · e.g. at bedtime

nodes.title: Myxedema coma: very rare
lines: obtundation, hypothermia · low BP, HR, Na, glucose · hypoventilation

nodes.title: No evidence treatment helps
lines: EXCEPT in pregnancy

nodes.title: Consider treating if
lines: TSH > 10 · anti-TPO positive · a therapeutic trial for possible symptoms

nodes.title: Levothyroxine, dosed on FREE T4
lines: ~pituitary lecture: replace the adrenal axis first

nodes.title: Methimazole FIRST line
lines: Graves can REMIT · ~4–6 weeks to euthyroid · favoured over PTU

nodes.title: Methimazole risks (rare)
lines: agranulocytosis · liver dysfunction · drug-induced lupus · birth defects

nodes.title: No remission → RAI
lines: may worsen eye disease

nodes.title: Surgery
lines: total thyroid-ectomy, rarely

nodes.title: RAI FIRST line
lines: permanent cure · ~6–12 weeks · ~10% need a 2nd dose

nodes.title: High risk of permanent hypothyroidism
lines: RAI NEVER in pregnancy

nodes.title: Surgery
lines: hemithyroidectomy (adenoma) · total (TMNG)

nodes.title: SUPPORTIVE only
lines: beta-blocker · NSAIDs, then glucocorticoids for the pain

nodes.title: Watch for the HYPOthyroid phase
lines: thyroiditis burns out

nodes.title: Exogenous
lines: remove the excess

nodes.title: TREAT if older and/or TSH lower
MONITOR if younger and/or borderline low

panels.title: Screen with a TSH when
items: personal or family autoimmune disease · Down or Turner syndrome
previous thyroid disease or therapy · drugs · pregnancy
suspected pituitary or hypothalamic disease: add FT4
rare: central HYPERthyroidism, TSH ↔/↑ with FT4 ↑

panels.title: Lowering production: which first?
items: methimazole first for GRAVES: it can remit
RAI first for toxic ADENOMA or TMNG, and Graves without remission
surgery rarely: large symptomatic goiter · suspected cancer · can't take drugs in pregnancy · storm refractory to treatment
supportive care for everyone: beta-blocker for palpitations, tachycardia, tremor

panels.title: Iodine cuts both ways
items: Wolff-Chaikoff: a normal gland CUTS production under an iodine load, then escapes
subclinical Hashimoto's may not escape → HYPOthyroid
Jod-Basedow: autonomous nodules or mild Graves use the iodine → HYPERthyroid
